findings.description: F001 says the listed guarded commands are the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 also add plan worktree create/remove behavior under the plan namespace. The contract separates guard, cleanup, and create rules, so the plan should explicitly classify those subcommands instead of relying on a contradictory completeness claim.

F002 requires gitignored content to block removal and be reported, but the enumerated tests do not pin an ignored-content refusal fixture. This is central to the preservation outcome and could regress while still satisfying the listed dirty and untracked tests.

F003 pins missing-config notices by default and divergent refusal during opt-in copy, but it does not clearly require default create-time detection and reporting of an already-present divergent allowlisted file. The objective says missing and divergent operator-local config must be declared explicitly.

The completion test requires fixture tests with zero live auditor calls, but F001 does not explicitly pin auditor stubbing or no-network assertions for audit and orchestrate dispatch entry-point tests. Those commands are the most likely to accidentally cross into live auditor behavior.

Override behavior is not pinned per refusal class. F001 clearly fail-closes corrupt registry loads, but also says an explicit override proceeds after evidence, leaving ambiguity over whether wrong path, unhealthy binding, swapped repo, indeterminate git state, and corrupt registry are all overrideable or whether some are absolute stops.

F002 does not specify or test what happens if registry binding deletion fails after the audit entry is flushed and after git worktree removal starts or succeeds. That leaves a cleanup path where the worktree can be gone but the registry still records a binding, which undermines the clean_removed_audited outcome.

The journey state names divergent_refused, but F003 says default create only detects and reports divergent allowlisted files, reserving refusal for copy-time overwrite attempts. The intended user-facing result for no-flag divergence is therefore ambiguous.

F001 declares the listed guarded commands to be the complete plan-mutating surface, but F002 and F003 introduce or modify plan worktree remove and plan worktree create, both of which mutate registry or worktree state. The plan needs an explicit decision that these commands are exempt from the wrong-worktree guard, or they need equivalent guard coverage.

F002 requires audit-first deletion, but the described audit record appears to encode a successful removal before the destructive git worktree remove step has actually succeeded. The registry-only completion path then relies on an audit log entry for successful removal, which can be ambiguous after partial failures.

F003 asserts that no symlinks are created in the new worktree, but it does not pin behavior when an allowlisted source file or preexisting target path is itself a symlink. That leaves a deterministic-rule gap for the no-symlinks-in-v1 policy and for copy-time overwrite refusal.
